q1: Give a fluid bolus and repeat tocilizumab for CRS. Monitor neuro checks. Await culture results before treating infection.
q2: Differential diagnosis: ICANS (most likely, day +6 after axi-cel with dysgraphia and aphasia); CNS relapse of lymphoma (parenchymal or leptomeningeal), important given his CNS-IPI 6 with kidney/adrenal involvement at diagnosis; CNS infection, including bacterial meningitis in a neutropenic patient and HSV or HHV-6 encephalitis; intracranial hemorrhage (platelets 44, INR 1.3); non-convulsive seizures or status epilepticus; sepsis-associated encephalopathy; metabolic causes (hyponatremia 131, hyperglycemia); drug effects; and posterior reversible encephalopathy.
q3: Investigations: urgent non-contrast CT head to exclude hemorrhage, then MRI brain with contrast (edema, leptomeningeal enhancement, lymphoma, encephalitis). EEG to exclude non-convulsive status. Lumbar puncture only after imaging and platelet transfusion to at least 50: opening pressure, cell count, protein, glucose, Gram stain and culture, HSV and HHV-6 PCR, cytology and flow cytometry. Blood: peripheral and line blood cultures, CBC, CMP, magnesium, phosphate, CRP, ferritin, fibrinogen, INR, lactate, ammonia, glucose monitoring; urine culture and chest X-ray for the fever source.
